- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish bias.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon after sharp price spikes; apply downward correction by 2–5% for the first 5–7 days post-spike.
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias — if forecast is above 95% of recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows rising positivity (e.g., 0.2→0.4→0.6), model often fails to catch momentum; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% per 2-day sentiment increase.
- Model underestimates true volatility in low-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment <0.1 for 3+ consecutive days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag by 2–4 days in true price direction — adjust forecast to match 10-day moving average of true values for lag correction.
